Postoperative Pain Assessment based on 
Photoplethysmography Analysis

Abstract. Knowing intraoperative pain is very important to prevent postoperative 
complication and delay in recovery. We analyzed P PG(Photoplethysmogram) 
waveform which is directly related to vasomotion to assess postoperative pain. 
Firstly, we found specific feature s of PPG signal such as peak points with 
preprocessing. Then, based on the clinical significance, we selected ten candidate 
parameters which might be affected by pain . Among those parameters, 
ACVsystole/HPH showed 82% of accuracy as alone parameter in dist inguishing 
existence of pain. Finally, with multiple features, we performed logistic 
regression analysis to improve classification accuracy. As a result of 100 times 
repetition, the classification accuracy was improved up to 86.36%. 
 
Keywords: Classification, pain assessment, photoplethysmography, 
postoperative pain 
 
 
1 Introduction 
 
Knowing the degree of pain during surgery is very important in dosing proper 
amount of anesthetic drugs. Generally, anesthesia is performed during surgery because 
severe pain from tissue damage is unavoidable. At the time, improper amount of drug 
usually causes side effects. For example, overdose of anesthetic drugs can cause delay 
in recovery, depress of circulatory system activity and physical performance.1 
Moreover, underdose of anesthetic drugs cause surgical nociceptive stimuli, stress 
responses and delay in recovery. 2 There has been a system for calculating proper 
amount of anesthetic drug, however, it still depends on subjective judgment of 
clinicians. Therefore, the objective pain quantification method is needed not only to 
prevent abuse of drugs but also to improve the prognosis of surgical patient.1,3 
In this research, we used photoplethysmogram(PPG), a biomedical signal that reflect 
the blood volum e changes in peripheral of body, as a promising source of pain 
quantification. Pain is caused by stimulation of the nociceptive receptors located in the 
peripheral nervous system and damage of the peripheral or central nervous system. At 
the time, the hyperkinetic fiber activation chemicals associated with vasomotor activity 
are secreted.4 
PPG is very simple and effective method to measure relative volume change of 
microvessels in tissues so it is a suitable biomedical signal for measuring changes in 
blood vessels caused by pain. 5 When analyzing the waveform obtained from the PPG 
analysis, the overall patient status of cardiovascular function can be easily identified. 
Also singularity analysis of waveform can confirm various clinical meanings such as 
changes in blood volume, artery compliance, maximum contraction interval, heart rate 
variation, changes in blood vessels during systolic and diastolic periods and 
vasodilatability.6 In this paper PPG analysis was performed to determine the presence 
or absence of pain.

2 Methods 
 
The overall procedure of this study is depicted in Fig.1. At first, we extracted specific 
features with preprocessing, then we obtained parameters that could reflect pain by 
combining various features. In pain classification , classification accuracy was 
evaluated for single and multiple parameters statistically. 
 
 
Fig.1. Overall procedure of this study 
 
 
2.1 Dataset 
 
Pre- and post-operative dataset was obtained from the Asan Medical Center Hospital 
in South Korea under an approved Asan Medical Center Hospital IRB protocol. In this 
research, we used 110 dataset of 55 subjects (28 males, 27 females, 51.1 ± 10.9 years 
old). 
 
2.2 Preprocessing 
 
Analyzing the PPG waveform, peak detection is essential. We used in house 
MATLAB(Mathworks, MA, USA) GUI to detect and correct peak locations. 7 
Generally, clinical data includes numerous artifacts caused by patient movement, 
electro-surgical artifacts or interventions. These artifacts could distort PPG waveform, 
and it make difficult to analyze PPG morphology. Therefore, we manually correct peak 
locations to eliminate misdetection or ectopic beat. 
 
2.3 Parameter Extraction 
 
Parameter extraction was performed with the procedure in Fig. 2. Totally, 10 
parameters from the PPG waveform, which are expected to have clinical relationship 
with a pain, were selected. The selected parameters were defined as the Peak to Peak 
Interval (PPIhead, PPIfoot), which is the time interval between the systolic and diastolic 
peaks, the height from the diastolic peak level to the near next systolic peak level as 
the Head Peak Height (HPH). AC Amplitude (ACA) which means the amplitude 
difference between systolic level and interpolation curve of adjacent diastolic peaks , 
Systolic AC Variation (ACVsystole) which means successive difference of systolic peak 
amplitudes and Diastolic AC Variation (ACVdiastole) which means successive difference 
of diastoli c peak amplitudes were also selected. Furthermore, we also calculated 
secondarily processed parameters with normalization; ACVsystole/HPH, ACVsystole/ACA, 
ACVdiastole/HPH and ACVdiastole/ACA.
